responses.reason: Utilities only moved $3,300, which is well under the $25,000 line, so a three-part story for that size change seems like more than the memo needs.
S12 mentions $12,800 of July fieldwork that will not be recorded until August, and that sounds like it belongs in July if the work happened then.
The prior column for account 5100 this month is $287,800, not $214,000, so comparing to $214,000 is comparing against the wrong month entirely.
S5 credits inbound freight rates for the cost of product sold change, but the memo itself says inbound freight sits outside cost of product sold.
S4 gives $74,900 for warehouse wages but the table shows account 6000 moved $79,400, so the two numbers do not line up.
S2 explains the $96,400 marketing number by pointing to a trade show in September, which is a strange reason for a July number to be high.
S6 blames the revenue drop on school nutrition seasonality without any account list or year over year numbers to back it up.
Inventory shrink jumped $62,300, which is a 700 percent move, and I cannot find one sentence anywhere in the memo about it.
The table shows software subscriptions moved $1,600 and 5.3 percent, not the $16,000 and 53 percent this challenge uses, so it clears neither leg.
Service revenue and repairs move in opposite directions the same month and nothing in the memo says whether the two are connected, so I would ask.
S8 already says the freight billed movement fails both legs of the threshold, so asking the controller for a closing entry seems like overkill for this one.
S3 gives $84,700 as the bad debt drop but the account only moved $52,500 according to the table, so the sentence and the table disagree.
Fleet fuel shows a $31,600 increase in the table, so S9 saying it declined is going in the wrong direction.
S10 says the repair program is done for the year, and then S11 describes a second phase of repairs the very next line, so they conflict.
